sourceObservations.observation: Viewed original PNG: four external source terminals, six switch contact circles, two open blades coupled by a double crossbar, one crossed-circle lamp, one four-lobed coil with a separate core bar, and the outer return conductor. Labels are +, -, and ~. Modern regularization: orthogonal conductors and dashed mechanical coupling distinguish coupling from an electrical short; blades remain open between the throws.

Viewed original PNG: one rectangular wire loop interrupted at two right-hand AC terminals, a four-lobed coil on the left, no core bar or lamp, and one ~ symbol between the terminals. Modern regularization changes only spacing and stroke consistency.

Viewed original PNG: shared upward value and rightward time axes, no ticks or grid, one smaller-amplitude current curve initially at a positive crest, a larger-amplitude voltage curve initially at zero and decreasing, and two label leaders. Voltage ends descending below zero, current ends after its next crest. Source labels u_L/i_L, u_L(t)/i_L(t), t and a round origin glyph. Modern regularization uses ideal harmonic curves; labels u,i,u(t),i(t) consistently denote this coil, without a redundant L subscript. Origin O is editorial modern notation, not an adjudication of the held O/0 source glyph. Neither axis is a measured shared-unit scale.
